doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Living near Juilliard and his first New York gig at Sugar Ray's
summary: Laws lived near the old Juilliard, where he met his first wife and Chick Corea. His first gig, on sax and flute in an organ trio at Sugar Ray's Lounge, supported him.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay. You’re in Juilliard. Your car got stolen.

Yeah, stolen, but that’s okay, because New York at that time, the subways were used a lot. That’s what I ended up doing. I lived right down the street from the old Juilliard. It was on 122nd Street and Amsterdam [Avenue], is where I lived. The old Juilliard was 122nd and Claremont [Avenue].
That’s where the Manhattan School of Music is?

That’s where it is now. The new Juilliard’s up there in Lincoln Center. Chick and I were – in fact, that’s where I met my first wife, too. She was a dancer there. But I didn’t really have that much use of a car in New York anyway. Nobody – where are you going to park it? Later on, I got a condo – they didn’t call them condos then. They

called them cooperatives. In that place, I was able to park my Porsche there, and it was covered, very inexpensive. For a long time I was able to park my cars that I had there. Before that, when I was in school, I didn’t really have that much of a use for a car. When I had my gigs – my first gig – I guess we want to get to that too, because that – my first gig I got after I was down to my last 50 bucks or so. My brother Johnny had come to New York with me from Houston. By the time I got my first gig, he got his first gig at the local grocery store, right down the street. I got a gig at Sugar Ray’s Lounge with an organ trio, playing saxophone and flute. That’s how I was able to support myself while attending Juilliard.
